transcript_tail.text: Running the close-work flow. Per your standing preference I'll take phases 1–5 end-to-end rather than stopping at each step, but I'll still gate on the readiness verdict and stop if anything's off. Starting with the review.

Phase 1 is clear. This is a **supervisor-managed `bridge-cse_*` worktree** (branch `worktree-bridge-cse_01Vm7LZtMvdnTdUBz1BnXRRm`), 2 commits ahead, clean tree, 45 files (all my doc/comment changes, −6471 lines). The main repo dir holds `main` at `767600cd` — which is **ahead of my base** (`ce9fe426`), so I need to check main didn't move under me before merging.

⚠️ Hold — main moved under me and it **conflicts with my premise.** Four security commits (#13/#49, #50) landed on main, and two of them touch files I changed:

- **`SECURITY_NEXT_STEPS.md`** — I *deleted* it; main just *modified* it while landing #49/#50. That's a delete/modify conflict, and more importantly: if main is actively ticking items off in that file, my "it's redundant, all items are tickets" rationale may be wrong.
- **`SecurityRouteAutomationTest.php`** — I edited a comment; main edited the allowlists (the #50 GET→POST work).

Let me look at exactly what main changed before I decide anything:

This is decisive. **Main is actively maintaining `SECURITY_NEXT_STEPS.md`** — the #50 merge edited it commit-by-commit, marking items DONE and leaving #49/#51/#53 as the live checklist for the in-flight security work stream. That directly contradicts my premise that it was dead/redundant. **Deleting it was wrong** — it would wipe an active working doc.

The `SecurityRouteAutomationTest.php` overlap is benign (main edited a different docblock/const than I did — clean auto-merge).

Let me also check whether main's *new* code (the #49/#13/#50 files) references any of the docs I deleted, which I wouldn't have de-linked:

Good — those origin/main hits are all the *pre-cleanup* references that my branch already fixes; main's security commits didn't introduce new ones. So the merge is clean **except** for the one real conflict: `SECURITY_NEXT_STEPS.md` (I delete it / main maintains it).

## Phase 4 verdict: NOT READY to merge as-is — one decision needed

Everything else is clean and ready:
- **Tests:** my changes are markdown + git-config + **comment-only** PHP edits (verified — no annotation/`@test`/logic lines touched). They can't affect test outcomes, so a suite run isn't warranted. `SecurityRouteAutomationTest.php` auto-merges cleanly (main edited a different const than I did).
- **TODO sweep:** both thread asks delivered; no in-code TODOs added; the 3 follow-ups are properly filed as #63/#64/#65. No tracking ticket or agent claim for this ad-hoc thread.
- **The rest of the deletions** don't conflict with main's new work.

The blocker is just `SECURITY_NEXT_STEPS.md`. My recommendation: **keep it** — main marked item #50 DONE in it days ago and #49/#51/#53 remain open there, so it's the live working checklist for the in-flight security stream, not dead weight. My "redundant" premise was wrong for this one file.
